x: Pride of place must go to our 4x440 yds Senior relay team of P.Pepe, C.Coxall, C.Jones and G.Leroy who, running in that order, defeated the holders, Epsom and Ewell Harriers, in 3m.28.3s.

Our track runners were more numerous, although in some of the events they were completely outclassed, notably the 880 yds, in which P. Pepe was unable to qualify for the final, and the 6 miles in which Eric Gebbett finished sixth.

The next event concerning the Bels was the 440 yds which was run as a straight final, and taking part was our 4 x 440 relay team. Alan Jackson and P. Pepe started rather fast into the mud while Brian Morris and Frank Wright went off steadily.

The unlucky trio were Peter Pepe 2:0.2, Pete Mitchell 2:2.1 and Randy Glen 2:3.1. In no way deterred by the reputations enjoyed by his opponents, Charlie Dabbs clung to the redoubtable Pirie and title-holder Ernie Earl sufficiently well to gain a notable 3rd place in the 3 miles, clocking 14:21.8---a personal best.
Earlier, Peter Pepe was narrowly defeated by the A.A.A.'s deathlaw Champion, Colin Andrews, in the quarter hurdles. The Army man clocked 57.3 to Peter's 57.4.
Peter Pepe went one better in the final of the 440 yards hurdles, and but for "fluffing" the last hurdle would have been second; despite this he still recorded 59.2 seconds.

After Terry Newell, Randy Glenn and Peter Pepe had run we were abreast of Blackheath, a good 15 yards clear of the remainder. Although he had run a half-mile heat and final during the afternoon, John Thresher took last stage.

Our South African member Blumberg was a clear winner in both sprints (10.8 and 23.8) and with Peter Pepe (52.6) and John Thresher (1:58.6) showing good early season form by winning the 440 and 880 yards respectively, we were well set to record a convincing win in our first fixture.

The 'quarter' developed into a two horse race between Worrall and Pete Pepe, whose form over the hurdles has of late been so encouraging. In the last few strides, however, Graham just had the edge and so took his second gold of the afternoon.
In the half mile Paul Ellis of Poly had the legs of John Thresher in the straight but Pete Pepe slipped nicely to third spot to help with the points situation.

CENTRE: Peter Pepe in full flight towards a fourth place in the 'Sward' 440 yds Hurdles final. BOTTOM LEFT: John Thresher and Gerry North bring the Bels home in first place in the "London Clubs' Two Mile" team final.
Peter Pepe finished 4th in the 440 yards Hurdles. Basil Blumberg who has been troubled with an injury, got into the final of the 220 yards hurdles but did not finish due to a recurrence of this.

Peter Pepe kept the flag flying by finishing 3rd in the one-lap hurdles in 57.4. John Thresher, although finishing 5th in the mile,won by Peter Keeling in 4:04.9, had the satisfaction of clocking 4:07.5, a time which he shared with international star John Boulter.

Notable senior performers for Belgrave, were Bill Kerr (4:18.2) who won the mile, and Peter Pepe (58.3) who took the 440 hurdles. The home club won the senior match with 100 points to Blackheath's 73 and our 70.
John Thresher, barely free from injury, was eliminated in his 1 mile heat with 4:10.1, as was Peter Pepe who recorded 56.8 in the 440 yards hurdles.
Brown, from a mark of 8 minutes, took first place, with Ted Pallent (9mins) second and Peter Pepe, better known as a hurdler, and receiving six minutes, third.
Peter Pepe (56.5) and Derek Wade (21'2½") provided sound support by finishing 5th in their events. All in all, not a season to be remembered.

Other noteworthy times were Mel Thorpe's 4:16.2 in the mile (best for some years) and John Dear's 4:25.0 (best ever). 100y A.3.C.Brooks 10.5 B.3.P.Pepe 11.3
John Bicourt and Peter Pepe both ran well,John being beaten by two good men in the 3000m SC and Pete finishing 5th in the high hurdles final.
Chris Martin and Philip Gee showed some good form in the sprints and Pete Pepe in his first race of the year clocked a good 16.4 for the high hurdles, finishing 3rd.
Our high hurdler Pete Pepe was 4th behind G.Tymms (Surrey) 14.8, Howell (HHH) 15.7 and Wilmshurst (Walton) 15.9 and was unlucky to be given 16.0 when he was inseparable with the 3rd man.

The High Hurdles were won for the fourth consecutive year by Pete Pepe but it was a much closer thing this time. Barry Townsend was with him over the first five flights but lost ground towards the finish.
